本当.etymology: The historical dictionary records 本当 in the sense of truth in a 1770 work, and a genuine or proper state in a 1785 work. These are cited attestations, not a claim that the word was coined in either year. The shorter spoken form ほんと is a sound change from ほんとう.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 本当

の.etymology: The noun-linking particle is already attested in the Kojiki of 712. It later also serves to turn a statement into something noun-like. The spoken ん before です in this taster is a contracted form of explanatory の, not the unrelated negative ending also written ん.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — の
Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ん

自分.etymology: The historical dictionary documents a self-referring use in a diary entry dated 1425 and also records its use for the person concerned. Its reference depends on the speaker and context. Here it refers to Megumi herself; the word does not have a fixed feminine meaning.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 自分

だ.etymology: The copula developed through contraction of である to であ and then だ. The dictionaries locate its development in the Muromachi period, especially eastern Japanese usage, and cite a 1473 example. Its connecting form is で, the form heard before いる in this taster.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — だ

いる.etymology: The older spelling is ゐる. Digital Daijisen identifies its original meaning as staying still in a low posture or sitting, in contrast with standing. It has developed the familiar meanings of being present or remaining in a state. This word is distinct from 要る, meaning to need.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 居る

なる.etymology: An old Japanese word: the historical dictionary cites forms in eighth-century texts for coming into being and changing into another state. Its modern meaning of becoming continues that change-of-state use. The lesson’s なった is the past form; it is not the different word 鳴る, to sound.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 成る

から.etymology: The particle has older route and starting-point uses. The historical dictionary treats its modern because-clause use as an Early Modern development and cites an example from around 1710. It lists competing accounts of the particle’s deeper origin; no single proposed prehistoric derivation is asserted here.

history.meaning: connects a reason to its result

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — から

出演する.etymology: This combines the verbal noun 出演 with する, to do. The historical dictionary cites 出演 in a 1904 novel for a public appearance or speech; the word also covers acting in film, theatre and broadcasting. This is an attested earlier use, not a verified date of coinage.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 出演

ほしい.etymology: The older adjective is ほし, with early attestations in the Kojiki and Manyoshu. The modern form is ほしい, also written 欲しい. The historical dictionary separately cites the pattern てほしい, wanting someone to do something, in a 1686 work.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 欲しい

です.etymology: The exact origin is disputed. Digital Daijisen lists proposals involving forms such as で候, でおはす, でございます and であります. It records the word from the Muromachi period onward, with general polite usage spreading in the late Edo and Meiji periods. Treating one proposed contraction as certain would overstate the evidence.

history.meaning: a form used in restricted dramatic and social settings
spreads as a general polite ending

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — です

アダルトビデオ.etymology: A Japanese compound made from the English-derived words adult and video. Shueisha’s katakana dictionary marks it as a Japanese formation.

sources.title: Shueisha imidas: Contemporary Katakana Dictionary — アダルトビデオ

に.etymology: This is an old Japanese particle with many functions. The historical dictionary cites eighth-century Manyoshu examples marking time, place and the setting of an action. The taster uses it to connect appearing to the kind of film. That modern use should not be reduced to a single universal English translation.

history.meaning: marks time, place and other relations

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — に

また.etymology: The adverb meaning again is attested in the Nihon Shoki of 720. It also developed uses meaning another occasion and also. The newly authored farewell またね draws on the sense of another meeting; it is not a quotation from the trailer.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 又

ね.etymology: The modern conversational particle is documented from late Edo speech; the historical dictionary cites a 1788 example. It softens an utterance or invites shared understanding. Dictionaries separately record an ancient request particle also pronounced ね; this entry does not claim that the modern farewell ending and that older use have an established single origin.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ね
